questions.q: Name two non-metals that are absolutely essential for keeping an animal alive.
questions.a: Oxygen and carbon. If a student only names one or confuses them with metals like iron, it reveals they have not yet distinguished between materials used for construction and materials used for survival.

questions.q: Why would a human be unable to survive for more than a few minutes without oxygen?
questions.a: Oxygen is required for cells to perform respiration and extract energy from food. A wrong answer (e.g., "it keeps us cool") reveals the student confuses a biological life-process requirement with simple physical properties like temperature.

questions.q: If you were to analyze the "backbone" of a human cell, which non-metal would you find at the center of every protein and DNA strand?
questions.a: Carbon. The student must identify carbon as the structural foundation. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks metals (like calcium) are the primary structural component of all organic molecules.

questions.q: Compare the role of iron in a building to the role of oxygen in a human body; how are their functions different?
questions.a: Iron provides static structural strength for external objects, while oxygen provides dynamic energy for internal biological survival. A wrong answer shows the student fails to distinguish between materials that are "used" to make objects and materials that "function" within a living system.

questions.q: Is it accurate to say that "metals are more important than non-metals because we build houses with them"? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, it is inaccurate because non-metals are essential for life itself. Without non-metals, there would be no living organisms to live in those houses. A wrong answer indicates the student values visible/tangible utility over invisible life-sustaining necessity.

questions.q: Imagine a planet where there is plenty of iron and gold but no carbon or oxygen. Could life exist there? Explain.
questions.a: No, because carbon is the backbone of all organic matter and oxygen is required for energy production. A poor answer fails to connect the biological requirement of these elements to the very definition of "life."

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Non-metals are materials that are essential for supporting biological life processes, serving as the ______ building blocks of cells and providing the gases necessary for energy production.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever wondered why we can build a house out of iron, but our own ______ are made of something completely different?
What is Non-metals? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Non-metals are materials that are essential for supporting biological life processes, serving as the fundamental building blocks of cells and providing the gases necessary for energy production.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Non-metals?
questions.a: Students often assume that because metals are hard, shiny, and used for construction, they are "more important" than non-metals.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to identify oxygen and carbon as non-metals and explain their specific roles in human life (respiration and structure of organic molecules).
